newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA should act to boost growth, cut jobless-Opp'n.
newsitem.headline: RBA should act to boost growth, cut jobless-Opp'n.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) should stimulate economic growth to help combat the country's chronic unemployment problem, the Labor opposition said on Wednesday.

Opposition Treasury Spokesman Gareth Evans said faster economic growth was needed to create jobs, and there was some agreement close to the bank's board that it should help employment rather than just fight inflation.
He said he hoped that feeling would prevail at the board's next meeting, due on June 3.
"The last best hope for generating some of that (economic) growth is in fact now with the Reserve Bank," Evans told the National Press Club.

"If the Reserve Bank is ever going to take seriously the second limb of its statutory charter -- have regard to full employment and general economic welfare as well as to the inflation target -- that time is frankly right now," he said.
"I know that a number of people close to the Reserve Bank board are persuaded that that's so, I simply hope that that argument will prevail in the meeting in a couple of week's time," Evans said.
The bank cut official cash rates 1.5 percentage points in three separate reductions in the second half of 1996.
Australia's official unemployment rate was 8.7 percent in April and has been stuck above 8.5 percent for more than a year.
The Liberal-National government has projected it will only fall to 8.25 percent year-average in the fiscal year from June.
